claim.point: The team decided to keep the sync job queue in SQLite (WAL mode) on the single sync host instead of moving it to the shared Postgres cluster.
claim.detail: It is simpler to operate and has been quiet since WAL; peak load is about 40 jobs a minute against a 2,000 a minute benchmark; Postgres would add a network hop and a two-week wait.

ask.point: Post the record to the team wiki.
ask.detail: The writer has no way to write to the wiki from the session, so the reader posts it.

stakes.point: The queue works on only one host, so if sync ever needs more than one worker host the team must revisit the decision and move the queue to Postgres.
stakes.detail: The capacity plan puts that at roughly 500 jobs a minute, possibly next year with the enterprise tier.
